notes: Access: shop.vtwonen.nl reached directly via curl_cffi impersonate=chrome124, robots.txt permits. Checked full collections.json (1250 collections, 5 pages) and pages.json (98 pages) for clearance/outlet terms (outlet, opruiming, clearance, final sale, end of line, last chance) in both handle and title, in Dutch and English - zero matches for 'outlet' or 'opruiming' anywhere on the site. The only discount-flavored listings found are: (1) a top-level nav item /collections/sale ('Sale', products_count~15787 per site metafield, exact count not verified since it was excluded) and (2) ~40 per-category '<category>-sale' collections (e.g. banken-sale, kasten-sale, sierkussens-sale). Applied the Sale-vs-Clearance test to /collections/sale: page <title> is 'Sale | Shop nu bij vtwonen!', <h1> is plain 'Sale', meta description carries no permanence language, and a full-text scan of the rendered page HTML found zero occurrences of 'opruiming', 'outlet', 'permanent', 'uitverkoop', or 'afprijzing'. No breadcrumb, on-page copy, or nav grouping treats this as clearance/end-of-line/outlet stock - it reads as a generic, ordinary promotional discount campaign spanning every category (consistent with the ~40 per-category '-sale' child collections, which look like a standard sitewide percent-off campaign structure, not a permanent-markdown outlet section). Per the brief's explicit instruction this is NOT classified as Clearance. Also checked Searchanise site search for 'opruiming' -> page returned a 'no results' state; 'outlet' returned generic keyword-match product results only (not a dedicated PLP). Conclusion: no genuine Clearance/Outlet-type merchandising PLP exists on this site as of this pass. This is a real absence, not a search-blind-spot - confirmed via full collection/page enumeration, not just site search.
